# Story 02 — Sign in against the real API and keep the session (Story: CRM-42)

## Prerequisites

- **IDENTITY-1-API (CRM-41)** shipped `POST /api/v1/sign-in` and `GET /api/v1/me` — see `api/openapi.json` lines 28–64 and `api/src/features/identity/identity.routes.js` line 12. Coordinate with the API owner only if the frozen 401 sameness or the 422 `fields` shape needs to change (it must not for this story).
- **LANGUAGES-1-WEB (CRM-35)** shipped the hardcoded-strings guard at `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`. Every new string added here must be added to **both** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` in the same commit — `defineLocale` at `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts:6` makes divergence a compile error.
- **PLATFORM-9-WEB** already ships `web/src/app/auth-context.tsx`, `web/src/shared/api/client.ts`, `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts`, and `web/src/testing/render.tsx`. **Use them; do not reimplement.**
- Read `.squad/plan-lessons.md` end to end before starting. L-15 (run `npm run build`, not only the suite) and L-16 (prove the guard fails on a regression) are load-bearing here.

---

## Story Goal

The sign-in screen calls the real API, stores the token the API issues, and takes the visitor to `/`. A refusal shows the API's `code` verbatim (no sentence written into the screen), clears the password field, and leaves the email in place. The submit button is disabled while the request is in flight, and the loading state comes from `useRequest`, not from a local boolean. A reload keeps the session (already true through `AuthProvider`; this story preserves the seam).

Explicitly **not in scope**: expired-token handling mid-session (IDENTITY-3-WEB), account management (IDENTITY-2-WEB), password change (IDENTITY-6/7-WEB), the desk shell (PLATFORM-12-WEB), the empty/loading/error design system (PLATFORM-16-WEB), and **any** API change. If the API surface looks short, note it and stop — do not add routes here.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** submit writes the literal `'stub-token'` into the auth context and navigates to `/`; no network call happens; the password stays in the field; there is no loading state; the screen shows a `stubNotice` explaining it is not real.
- **New behaviour:**
  - Submit calls `POST /api/v1/sign-in` with `{ email, password }` via `request()`.
  - On 200, pass the returned `token` (**not** any local fabrication) to `signIn(token)`, then `navigate('/', { replace: true })`.
  - On any error, keep the email, **clear the password** (`setPassword('')`), and show the API's `code` verbatim (see string rules below).
  - The submit button is `disabled` when `status === 'loading'`; the loading state comes from `useRequest`, never from a local `useState<boolean>`.
  - Nothing outside `web/src/testing/render.tsx` may write `'stub-token'`.

**String rules — no sentences in the screen.** The screen renders `t.signIn.errors[error.code]` (or a `t.signIn.errors.default` fallback) so translations live entirely in the resource files, in both languages, per the intake's explicit instruction. The screen source contains no `"Wrong email or password"`-style prose.

## Frontend Tasks

_No backend changes required._ The API this screen calls is already shipped by CRM-41 (`api/openapi.json` lines 28–64, `api/src/features/identity/identity.routes.js:12`). If a gap is discovered while implementing, stop and raise it; do not extend the API in this story.

### 1 — Rewrite `SignInPage` to call the API

**File:** `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx` (replace body).

Structure:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';

import { useAuth } from '../../app/auth-context';
import { useTranslation } from '../../shared/i18n';
import { useRequest } from '../../shared/hooks';
import { request } from '../../shared/api/client';
import { ApiError } from '../../shared/api/errors';
import { Button, Card, Field, Heading, Stack, Text } from '../../shared/ui';

type SignInResponse = { token: string; user: { id: string; role: string; name: string } };

export function SignInPage() {
  const { signIn } = useAuth();
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('');
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('');
  const { status, error, run } = useRequest<SignInResponse>();

  async function onSubmit(event: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault();
    try {
      const { token } = await run(() =>
        request<SignInResponse>('/sign-in', {
          method: 'POST',
          body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
        }),
      );
      signIn(token);                       // the API's token, verbatim
      navigate('/', { replace: true });
    } catch {
      setPassword('');                     // criterion 2: clear on refusal
      // run() has already set status='error' and error=<ApiError>
    }
  }

  // …render, unchanged in structure, plus:
  //   <Button type="submit" disabled={status === 'loading'}>{t.signIn.submit}</Button>
  //   {error ? <Text variant="error">{t.signIn.errors[error.code] ?? t.signIn.errors.default}</Text> : null}
  // …and remove the <Text variant="muted">{t.signIn.stubNotice}</Text> line.
}
```

Constraints:

- **Do not** introduce a `useState<boolean>` for loading. The button's `disabled` is derived from `status` (or `status === 'loading'`).
- **Do not** translate `error.code` inline in JSX — read it out of `t.signIn.errors`.
- Keep the primitive assembly (`Card`, `Field`, `Heading`, `Stack`, `Button`, `Text`); do not add new CSS, spacing or radii — see the comment already at `SignInPage.tsx` lines 8–9.
- Path passed to `request()` is `/sign-in` (client prefixes `/api/v1`; see `web/src/shared/api/client.ts:1`).
- Keep `autoComplete="username"` and `autoComplete="current-password"` on the fields (already at lines 36, 46). Do not alter `id`, `name`, `type` attributes — the guard at `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts:34–43` deliberately does not flag them.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **401 UNAUTHENTICATED** — wrong password, unknown email, disabled account. The API answers them identically on purpose (`api/openapi.json:39`). The screen must not attempt to distinguish; it renders `t.signIn.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED` and clears the password field.
- **422 VALIDATION_FAILED** — well-formed JSON but wrong shape (empty email/password). Body carries `fields` names (`api/openapi.json:42`). The screen renders `t.signIn.errors.VALIDATION_FAILED`; do **not** render field values. `error.fields` may be logged/inspected but nothing values-related is rendered.
- **Network failure or `fetch` reject** — `request()` throws `ApiError({ status: 0, code: 'INTERNAL', … })` (client.ts:31). `useRequest` funnels non-`ApiError` throws into the same code (useRequest.ts:31–34). The screen renders `t.signIn.errors.INTERNAL`.
- **Unknown/new API code** — the API's frozen catalogue is at `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts:5–13`, but the wire may still return something the screen has not mapped. Use `t.signIn.errors[error.code] ?? t.signIn.errors.default` so the screen never renders `undefined`.
- **Double-submit** — the second click while `status === 'loading'` must not fire a second request. Enforced by the `disabled` on the button; belt-and-braces, the `latest` ticket in `useRequest` drops stale answers if it happens through another path.
- **Storage blocked / private window** — `signIn()` swallows the write failure (auth-context.tsx:38–42); the tab remains signed in, a reload does not. Unchanged behaviour; do not regress it.
- **Reload with a stored token** — `readStoredToken()` runs synchronously in `useState(readStoredToken)` (auth-context.tsx:35). This is what makes a reload keep the session. Nothing in this story may replace it with a `useEffect`.
- **RTL language** — `renderWithProviders({ language: 'ar' })` continues to render Arabic labels (`routing.test.tsx:41–45`). Error strings added in Arabic must render RTL without extra work; verify with the test in task 5.

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema or config changes. The only user-visible change is that the sign-in button now actually calls the API and can fail.
- **Rollback:** revert the three files (`SignInPage.tsx`, `en.ts`, `ar.ts`) and the routing-test edit. The auth-context comment change is cosmetic and safe either way. There is no half-applied state to worry about because nothing persists across the boundary except the token in `localStorage`, which is opaque to the schema.
